Things you can do to help menopause
and perimenopause symptoms
Lifestyle changes for perimenopause and
menopause
Eating well, exercising and looking after your mental wellbeing can help with symptoms
during perimenopause and menopause.
It can also help you keep as well as possible in the future.
(Link: www.nhs.uk/)
Do
try to get plenty of rest, including keeping to regular sleep routines
try to eat a healthy, balanced diet
eat calcium-rich food like milk, yoghurt and kale, if you can, to keep your
bones healthy
exercise regularly, with focus on weight-bearing exercises to build strength as
this can help protect against weakening bones
try relaxing things such as yoga, tai chi or meditation
talk to other people going through the same thing, like family, friends or
colleagues
talk to a doctor before taking herbal supplements or complementary
medicines
talk to a doctor about hormonal contraception if you need to – HRT is not
contraception
Things you can do to help menopause and perimenopause symptoms - NHS
https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/menopause-and-perimenopause/things-you-can-do/
1/4

Other ways to help perimenopause and
menopause symptoms
How to ease mood changes
It's common to have mood swings, low mood and anxiety around the time of the menopause
and perimenopause.
Try to:
get as much rest as you can
exercise regularly
do relaxing activities
Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) (Link: www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cognitivebehavioural-therapy-cbt/) is a type of talking therapy that can help with a low mood and
feelings of anxiety. It can also help with sleep problems.
How to ease hot flushes and night sweats
You can try:
wearing lightweight clothing
keeping your bedroom cool at night
taking a cool shower, using a fan or having a cold drink
finding ways to reduce your stress level (Link: www.nhs.uk/mental-health/self-help/guidestools-and-activities/tips-to-reduce-stress/)
to avoid or reduce potential triggers, such as spicy food, caffeine, hot drinks, smoking and
alcohol
to exercise (Link: www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/) regularly
to keep to a healthy weight (Link: www.nhs.uk/live-well/healthy-weight/)
Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) (Link: www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cognitivebehavioural-therapy-cbt/) can also help manage hot flushes.
How to ease vaginal dryness
There are vaginal moisturisers or lubricants you can get without a prescription at a pharmacy.
Don’t
do not smoke as this can make menopause symptoms worse
try not to drink more than the recommended alcohol limit – it may affect your
symptoms
Things you can do to help menopause and perimenopause symptoms - NHS
https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/menopause-and-perimenopause/things-you-can-do/
2/4

You can talk to a pharmacist, in private, if you'd like help to decide which moisturiser is right
for you.
If you're having sex and using condoms, do not use an oil-based lubricant as this can damage
condoms. Water-based lubricants are available.
There are other treatments for vaginal dryness that a doctor can prescribe, such as HRT
(hormone replacement therapy) or hormonal treatment (creams, pessaries, gel or vaginal
rings).
Find out about treatment for vaginal dryness (Link: www.nhs.uk/medicines/hormonereplacement-therapy-hrt/vaginal-oestrogen/).
Protecting against weak bones
You can try to:
exercise regularly, particularly focusing on strength exercises (Link: www.nhs.uk/livewell/exercise/strength-exercises/), where your feet and legs support your weight (like
walking, running or dancing) and resistance exercises (for example, using weights)
eat a healthy diet that includes plenty of fruit, vegetables and sources of calcium, such as
milk, yoghurt and kale
get some sunlight on your skin as this triggers the production of vitamin D (Link:
www.nhs.uk/conditions/vitamins-and-minerals/vitamin-d/), which can help keep your
bones healthy
take vitamin D supplements
stop smoking and cut down on alcohol
Taking HRT can also reduce the risk of osteoporosis.
Find out more about preventing osteoporosis (Link:
www.nhs.uk/conditions/osteoporosis/prevention/)
Find out more
Reducing health risks after menopause on the British Nutrition Foundation
website (Link: https://www.nutrition.org.uk/nutritionfor/women/menopause/reducing-health-risks-after-the-menopause-with-nutritionand-diet/)

84KB) (Link: https://www.womens-health-concern.org/wpcontent/uploads/2023/06/31-WHC-FACTSHEET-Weight-Gain-and-menopause-
